patient_information: A 30-year-old woman from Santa Cruz, Bolivia, who arrived in Spain 4 months prior, grew up in a rural area, and expresses the wish to become pregnant.
chief_complaint: A 2-year history of progressive dyspnoea at moderate exertion (New York Heart Association grade II) along with self-limiting palpitations.
history_of_present_illness: The patient has a 2-year history of progressive dyspnoea and palpitations, with no other relevant medical history or current medication.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Born in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, grew up in a rural area during childhood, and arrived in Europe 4 months prior to presentation.
vitals: Blood pressure 110/65 mmHg, pulse 40 bpm and regular, SpO2 99% on ambient air.
physical_exam: Cardiac sounds are clear with no murmurs, chest is clear, no peripheral oedema, and jugular venous pressure is not raised.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count and basic blood chemistry tests were normal; ECG showed sinus bradycardia with right bundle branch block; chest radiograph showed moderate cardiomegaly; serological testing confirmed Chagas disease with positive IgG antibodies against Trypanosoma cruzi; echocardiography revealed a hypertrophic left ventricle without obstruction.
differential_diagnosis: Screening for active and latent tuberculosis, HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, strongyloidiasis, and Chagas disease in a recent migrant from Bolivia.
management_and_clinical_course: Treated with benznidazole 5 mg/kg per day for 60 days; developed a pruritic maculopapular rash and mild eosinophilia which resolved after corticosteroids and antihistamines, allowing completion of the benznidazole course; follow-up 5 years later showed stable cardiac function and she gave birth to a healthy child.
